name: Prostatilen

lead: Prostatilen is a peptide extract from cattle prostate, developed in the Soviet Union and used in Russia and nearby countries for prostatitis and prostate enlargement. Longevity circles list it with other Khavinson bioregulators as a general-health option. It is a urology product, not a cosmetic one.

The chain runs from a tissue-specific prostate extract to urological support to general health. Early-1990s Russian reports looked at prostatitis, rat studies report changes in prostate size and oxidative-stress markers, and a 2026 paper examined prostate-derived peptide preparations and erectile function in men with chronic prostatitis.

paras: Clinically it is given in courses for prostate conditions in post-Soviet countries. In longevity circles it appears alongside other bioregulator peptides.
Safety information comes mostly from regional studies; two older mouse studies examined mutagenicity. It is not a Western-approved drug, and independent trials are not documented.

angle.text: Prostatilen is a bovine prostate extract used in post-Soviet urology for prostatitis and enlargement, and mentioned in bioregulator discussions as a general-health option. Data is mostly Russian-language clinical work; no appearance use is described.

lead: Prostatilen is a peptide preparation extracted from the prostate glands of cattle. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the mid-1980s and has been used in Russia, Ukraine and other post-Soviet countries for chronic prostatitis and benign prostatic hyperplasia, according to Grokipedia [1]. It belongs to the family of organ-derived peptide bioregulators, or cytomedins, associated with Vladimir Khavinson's research group [2].

Published human studies are largely Russian-language reports from the early 1990s on prostatitis, plus experimental work in rats and mice [3][4][5][6][7]. A 2026 paper examined prostate-derived complex peptide preparations and erectile function in men with chronic prostatitis [8]. No Western randomised trials are listed in the available literature.
Prostatilen is a urology product rather than a cosmetic one. It appears in longevity-peptide discussions alongside other Khavinson preparations [2].
infobox: Chronic prostatitis, benign prostatic hyperplasia (post-Soviet states) [1]
Marketed in Russia/Ukraine; not a Western-approved drug

paras: According to Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, Prostatilen consists of low-molecular-weight peptides obtained by ultrafiltration of a bovine prostate extract, and is supplied as suppositories and as a powder for intramuscular injection [1]. Variants combining the extract with zinc or arginine are also described there [1].

Early Russian-language papers from 1991 report its use in patients with prostatic diseases and chronic prostatitis, including prostatitis accompanied by sexual dysfunction [9][6][7]. Grokipedia states that early trials reported symptom improvement in most patients, a claim it does not tie to controlled data [1]. A review by Khavinson's group lists Prostatilen among bioregulators with clinical efficacy in prevention and treatment [2]. A 2026 report examined prostate-derived peptide preparations and erectile function in chronic prostatitis [8].
Reports are mostly from the developers' regional literature, and independent replication is not documented.

In rats with experimentally induced prostatic hyperplasia, Prostatilen was reported to prevent increases in prostate size and to alter oxidative-stress markers, with an effect comparable to a saw palmetto extract in one study [10][2]. A 1995 report in male rats described stimulating effects on spermatogenesis and testicular androgen function [3]. Two 1990s mouse studies examined its mutagenicity and how vitamin C or immobilisation modified it [4][5].
